wiki_only_topics.topic: Ray tracing and the Eikonal equation
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: In modern applied physics and engineering physics, the term also encompasses numerical solutions to the Eikonal equation.

wiki_only_topics.topic: Special ray types in optical modelling
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: A skew ray is a ray that does not propagate in a plane that contains both the object point and the optical axis (meridional or tangential plane).

The marginal ray (sometimes known as an a ray or a marginal axial ray) in an optical system is the meridional ray that starts from an on-axis object point (the point where an object to be imaged crosses the optical axis) and touches an edge of the aperture stop of the system.
A paraxial ray is a ray that makes a small angle to the optical axis of the system and lies close to the axis throughout the system.
A guided ray, bound ray, or trapped ray is a ray in a multi-mode optical fiber, which is confined by the core.
